Authors: Fan S.; Cui Z.; Chen X.; Liu X.; He L.; Yan T.; Li H.; Wang Y.; Yao C.; Xiao M.; Sun T.; Xing F.
Title: Plug-and-Play Enabled Modular Nanosatellite Platform Architecture: Design, Implementation, and On-Orbit Performance Validation
Source title: Proceedings of the International Astronautical Congress, IAC
Abstract: Nanosatellites, represented by CubeSats, have attracted growing attention owing to their short development cycles, low cost, and high functional density; however, their core subsystems and architecture still suffer from challenges in reliability, universality, and the trade-off between high-precision control and flexible integration, limiting applications in advanced space missions. To address these issues, this paper proposes a modular nanosatellite platform architecture based on plug-and-play (PnP) units. These units include the PnP-integrated attitude determination and control system (ADCS), and the telemetry & orbit determination system. The architecture incorporates two core innovations that achieve PnP functionality without compromising precision. First, for precision guarantee, the PnP-iADCS compactly integrates multiple high-performance components into a standard 1U form factor. This form factor has a dimension of 96×96×100 mm and a mass of 1349 grams. The integrated components include dual deployable star trackers, which achieve an attitude measurement accuracy of 3 arcseconds at the 3σ confidence level; a micro-digital multiple apertures sun sensor, which has an angular uncertainty of 3.1 arcseconds at the 3σ confidence level; dual three-axis gyroscopes with an angle random walk of 0.01°/√h; dual three-axis magnetometers; four reaction wheels, each with a torque of 2.5 millinewton-meters; three magnetorquers; a high-precision Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) module; and an onboard computer (OBC). Second, for standardized PnP integration, a unified interface system is designed, which includes a unified 5V electrical supply and signaling scheme, and a PnP communication protocol that enables 2-second module recognition and activation. Additionally, a unified rigid-body dynamics framework is established to fuse real-time orbital data and identified inertial parameters, ensuring stable control performance post-module replacement. Based on this architecture, the NanoSat-III A/B and NanoSat-IV A/B satellites (equipped with PnP-iADCS) were successfully launched in 2024; they maintained 3" attitude determination accuracy and 0.02° pointing accuracy during 6 months of on-orbit operation, while shortening the satellite integration cycle compared to traditional customized designs. Author full names: Luccisano, Giacomo; Salas Cordero, Sophia; Gateau, Thibault; Viola, Nicole
Title: Open-Source Data Formalization through Model-Based Systems Engineering for Concurrent Preliminary Design of CubeSats
Abstract: Market trends in the space sector suggest a notable increase in satellite operations and market value for the coming decade. In parallel, there has been a shift in the industrial and academic sectors from traditional Document-Based System Engineering to Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) combined with Concurrent engineering (CE) practices. Due to growing demands, the drivers behind this change have been the need for quicker and more cost-effective design processes. A key challenge in this transition remains to determine how to effectively formalize and exchange data during all design stages and across all discipline-specific tools; as representing systems through models can be a complex endeavor. For instance, during the Preliminary design (PD) phase, the integration of system models with external mathematical models for simulations, analyses, and system budgeting is crucial. The introduction of CubeSats and their standard has partly addressed the question of standardization and has aided in reducing overall development time and costs in the space sector. Nevertheless, questions about how to successfully exchange data endure. This paper focuses on formalizing a CubeSat model for use across various stages of the PD phase. The entire process is conducted with the exclusive use of open-source tools, to facilitate the transparency of data integration across the PD phases, and the overall life cycle of a CubeSat. The paper has two primary outcomes: (i) developing a generic CubeSat model using Systems modeling language (SysML) that includes data storage and visualization through the application of Unified modeling language (UML) stereotypes, streamlining in parallel information exchange for integration with various simulation and analysis tools; (ii) creating an end-to-end use case scenario within the Nanostar software suite (NSS), an open-source framework designed to streamline data exchange across different software during CE sessions. A case study from a theoretical academic space mission concept is presented as the illustration of how to utilize the proposed formalization, and it serves as well as a preliminary validation of the proposed formalization. The proposed formalization positions the CubeSat SysML model as the central data source throughout the design process. It also supports automated trade-off analyses by combining the benefits of SysML with effective data instantiating across all PD study phases.
